title.narrative: Second Health Care in the Central Highlands Project

description.narrative: The project will help the government to further reduce maternal and child mortality by addressing access to and quality gaps in commune health stations (CHSs) and hospitals and by strengthening provincial health management in five provinces, thereby targeting the poor, ethnic groups, and women and children in particular.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Increased use of health services, in particular maternal and child health services in district hospitals, ICPs, and CHSs

Inpatient visits per person per year to district hospitals and ICPs increased by 20% (2014 baseline: 0.065), with data in the poorest districts and disaggregated by age, gender, and ethnic group. Progress/Status: On track. Inpatient visits per person per year to district hospitals and ICPs reached 0.099, a 52% increase. Data Source: District health office reports from the health information system
General Statistics Office
Viet Nam living standards households surveys Actual value:

Under-5 child malnutrition (underweight) reduced by 20% (2014 baseline: 22.6%). Progress/Status: Achieved. Under-5 child malnutrition was reduced to 16.5% from 22.6% in 2014, a 27% reduction. Data Source: District health office reports from the health information system
General Statistics Office
Viet Nam living standards households surveys Actual value:

Proportion of ethnic women deliveries assisted by skilled staff increased to 85%. (2014 baseline: 82.5%). Progress/Status: Achieved. Proportion of ethnic women deliveries assisted by skilled staff reached 90%. Data Source: District health office reports from the health information system
General Statistics Office
Viet Nam living standards households surveys Actual value:

Outpatient visits per person per year to district hospitals and CHSs increased by 30% (2014 baseline: 0.47 and 0.67, respectively); with data in the poorest districts and disaggregated by age, gender, and ethnic group. Progress/Status: On track. Outpatient visits per person per year to district hospitals reached 0.78 from 0.47 in 2014, a 66% increase. Outpatient visits to CHSs decreased to 0.51 per person per year (a 24% reduction from baseline of 0.67). The decrease is due to the following: (i) people tend to seek health services at district health facilities as the transportation from the commune to the district has become more convenient; and (ii) following Vietnam's amended health insurance law, people registered under primary healthcare provider at CHSs can go to other CHSs or direct to the district hospitals within the province for equal health insurance reimbursement. Thus, people tend to choose district health facilities with higher professional qualifications, better facilities than commune level for outpatient care. Nevertheless, this is a positive signal because people will be treated at the district level with better service quality. MOH is also advocating to strengthen healthcare at commune level, focusing on preventive health mainly. Data Source: District health office reports from the health information system
